A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the majority of patients treated for TB are low-moderate smokers and that the cessation messages used in this study were effective in reducing the level of smoking among those who continue to smoke post treatment, and in maintaining abstinence in those who quit during treatment.

the TB clinic is an appropriate setting to introduce a smoking cessation message to TB patients, and that a TB-specific message can be as effective as the standard message in reducing smoking during and following treatment for TB.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the cessation of smoking is possible for patients treated for TB, even those who smoke heavily, and even in the absence of pharmacotherapy.
low-moderate smoking is a significant challenge to smoking cessation interventions in LMICs and should be addressed in future studies.

the majority of patients who smoke heavily during TB treatment are able to quit entirely and sustain their abstinence for six months or more post-treatment, even in the absence of a smoking cessation intervention.
